newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settlers condemn Hebron deal, vow to stay.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settlers condemn Hebron deal, vow to stay.

text.p: Grim-faced Jewish settlers in Hebron blasted a deal on Wednesday to hand over most of the town to the PLO as capitulation to "terror" but vowed not to budge from the heart of the West Bank city.
"Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who argued in his own book that you can't bend to terror, has himself capitulated to terror," Noam Arnon, a leader of Hebron's 400 Jews, told Reuters.

Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Wednesday sealed a long-elusive deal to launch Palestinian self-rule in 80 percent of the volatile town, holy to Jews and Moslems as the burial site of the biblical Abraham.

"The reality here will be very, very difficult. Hundreds of armed terrorists will enter the city and occupy it," Arnon said, pulling a hood over his head as cold rain pelted a tiny Jewish enclave in the heart of the town of 100,000 Arabs.
"In the next stage they will want to slaughter the Jewish community in Hebron."
Jewish settlers in Hebron for months waged a public campaign to pressure Netanyahu to scuttle the Hebron deal he inherited from the centre-left government he ousted in May.
They said Netanyahu, elected on a platform opposing the exchange of Israeli-occupied land for peace, had betrayed them.
"We expected he would stand up for the principles," settler spokesman David Wilder told Reuters. "He has given in on just about everything and we're very upset."
Israeli troops are to remain in 20 percent of Hebron to guard the town's tiny number of Jews after the pullback but settlers maintain the entry of armed PLO police will endanger their existence.
"I'm sure that things will explode," Wilder said.
He said Hebron's Jews would not cooperate with the Palestinian Authority. "I do not see us sitting down at a table with people who not only have murdered in the past but want to kill us also."
Asked about Palestinian fears armed Jewish settlers would try to attack Arabs in an attempt to sabotage PLO rule, Wilder said the interests of Hebron's Jews were not served by such tactics.
"But I'm much more concerned about attacks on us than about attacks by Jews on Arabs," he added.
Noam Friedman, a right-wing religious Jew from a settlement near Jerusalem, wounded seven Arabs in a shooting spree in Hebron's open-air vegetable market on New Year's Day.
In 1994, U.S.-born Baruch Goldstein from nearby Kiryat Arba settlement massacred 29 Palestinian worshippers in Hebron's al-Ibrahimi mosque.
Wilder said he feared Islamic militants would retaliate against Hebron's Jews "sooner or later".
But the settlers said they would find a way to live with the new realities in Hebron and vowed never to leave the city.

"People here are not depressed. We will stay here to establish the community here, to strengthen it and to enlarge it in order to prove the Jewish people has not abandoned Hebron, its homeland and its values," Arnon said.
"We are ready to stand here against this cruel Arab and Islamic terror...this struggle will continue and I believe we will succeed."
